records.title: Add a Turso-backed Graph builtin
records.body:
## Context

Verglas needs an eighth prebuilt Worker/Durable Object product for bounded property-graph storage and traversal. Each named graph is owned by one serialized Durable Object and its embedded Turso database.

Turso's published knowledge-graph pattern models graph structure relationally with node and edge tables. The graph product uses ordinary covering B-tree adjacency indexes. It does not add a native graph engine, external service, Cypher/Gremlin parser, in-memory authority, Vamana state, or a custom Turso index method.

## Contract

A Worker declares:

```toml
[[graphs]]
binding = "GRAPH"
graph_name = "knowledge"
```

The binding exposes:

```js
await env.GRAPH.upsertNodes(nodes);
await env.GRAPH.upsertEdges(edges);
await env.GRAPH.getNodes(ids);
await env.GRAPH.getEdges(ids);
await env.GRAPH.deleteNodes(ids);
await env.GRAPH.deleteEdges(ids);
await env.GRAPH.neighbors(nodeId, options);
await env.GRAPH.shortestPath(fromId, toId, options);
await env.GRAPH.describe();
```

Nodes contain `id`, `kind`, and optional JSON `properties`. Edges contain `id`, `from`, `to`, `kind`, optional finite `weight`, and optional JSON `properties`. Upserts replace records in full. Mutations return a durable replay-stable `{ mutationId }`.

Traversal options support `direction` (`out`, `in`, or `both`), optional edge kinds, bounded depth and result limit, and filters over explicitly indexed node and edge properties. Neighbor and shortest-path results are deterministic.

## Turso layout

Use `graph_nodes` and `graph_edges` tables plus covering indexes on:

- `(from_id, kind, to_id, id)`
- `(to_id, kind, from_id, id)`
- `(kind, id)` for nodes

Store mutation receipts and property-index declarations in the same database. Property-index create/list/delete operations are management routes outside the tenant binding. Validated property names may create matching Turso JSON expression indexes; all property values remain SQL parameters.

Pinned Turso 0.7.2 rejects recursive CTEs, so multi-hop traversal uses one explicit bounded iterative path over indexed adjacency seeks. There is no recursive-CTE fallback. Hard ceilings cover depth, frontier size, visited nodes, scanned edges, request bytes, and response size. Budget exhaustion fails without a partial success.

Deleting a node explicitly deletes incident edges in the same transaction. Do not depend on implicit foreign-key cascade behavior.

## Work

- Add `system/graph` as a prebuilt Worker/Durable Object product.
- Add strict `graphs` manifest parsing and a JavaScript Graph binding.
- Add Graph artifact selection and routing to the gateway.
- Add actual embedded Turso tests proving adjacency query plans use the outbound and inbound indexes.
- Add graph CRUD, restart, rollback, traversal, property filter, injection, cycle, deterministic ordering, and hard-ceiling tests.
- Update architecture and product inventory documentation from seven products to eight.
- Append worklog entries for every touched crate, SDK, and system product.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tests are written first and fail for the missing graph binding/product behavior.
- Bundled Worker code uses `env.GRAPH` directly with no Verglas-specific application transport.
- Node and edge upserts replace records in full and exact retries return the same durable mutation id.
- Edge insertion rejects missing endpoints without partial writes.
- Node deletion atomically removes incident edges.
- Outbound, inbound, both-direction, cyclic, multi-hop, and shortest-path fixtures are correct and deterministic.
- Node and edge property predicates are applied before frontier expansion and only declared properties may filter.
- Filter values cannot inject SQL and graph/property identifiers cannot become unchecked SQL text.
- Actual pinned Turso `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` output proves both adjacency indexes are selected.
- Configuration, mutations, graph state, and property-index declarations survive reopen; failed events leave no partial graph or receipt.
- Every traversal ceiling fails explicitly rather than returning incomplete results.
- No custom graph index, recursive CTE compatibility path, Cypher/Gremlin surface, or external graph authority is introduced.
- Focused tests, `just lint`, and `cargo test --workspace` pass.

records.title: Request: cut a release of the Scala 3 line (87 commits since v4.8.6, includes the #720 compile-time fix)
records.body:
## Summary

`master` is 87 commits ahead of `v4.8.6`, which was cut on 2024-10-30. Would the
maintainers consider cutting a release of the Scala 3 line?

The commit that motivates the request is #720, *perf(macros): reduce redundant
implicit searches in ctx.run() pipeline*, merged 2026-02-24. It closes #619,
where the same symptom was reported as very slow compilation of modules with
many `ctx.run()` call sites.

## Why it matters downstream

We run a Scala 3 / ZIO 2 codebase where every repository is a static Quill
query — 113 files with `ctx.run()` call sites across 14 sbt modules. Compiling
them is dominated by the `inlining` phase, and inside it by the
`GenericEncoder`/`GenericDecoder` implicit searches that #720 removes.

Measured A/B of the full gate, `sbt "clean; testFull"`, on a 16 vCPU machine
with the sbt action cache and every `target/` cleared before each run and
dependency resolution warmed beforehand:

| quill | sbt elapsed |
|---|---|
| 4.8.6 | 412 s |
| master | 281 s |
| 4.8.6, repeated last | 414 s |

Identical work on both sides: 1484 sources compiled, 2869 tests passing, no
errors. The baseline was run first and last so warm-up could be ruled out. That
is a 32% reduction of a whole build-and-test cycle from one merged commit, and
it is larger on hosts where compilation is a bigger share of the total.

## Why the snapshot does not cover it

Snapshots are published on every push, so the fix is technically obtainable:

```text
dev.zio:quill-jdbc-zio_3:0.0.0+1-76803759-SNAPSHOT
```

Three practical problems keep that out of a build. The coordinate is mutable, so
it is not a reproducible input. Snapshot retention removes it — only three
currently exist on Central, one per recent commit. And the version is stamped
`0.0.0+1-<sha>`, which sorts below every real version, because the CI checkout
has no tags for dynver to describe; `actions/checkout` needs `fetch-depth: 0`
(and tags) for dynver to produce a meaningful snapshot version. That last one
looks like a small, independent fix worth making regardless of the release
question.

## What we did meanwhile

We republish `master` to a private registry under a pinned version so the fix is
usable, and we would drop that the day a release exists. Happy to help test a
release candidate against a real ZIO/Quill codebase if that is useful.

records.title: 🧪 [Infra] Story · Unit test runner for src/ with coverage on the wave-0/1 blast radius
records.body:
## 🎯 Goal
Testing a pure function in this repo currently means booting Chromium. That makes the cheap tests expensive, loads the e2e suite with work it should not carry, and — the reason this is P1 — it means the three foundational refactors queued behind it (#1515 migrations, #1549 tenant key, #1563 permission model) have no way to be proven correct except by clicking through a browser. A unit runner turns "risky refactor we avoid" into "refactor with a red/green answer in four seconds".

## 🔍 Current state
- `package.json:13-40` — no vitest, no jest, no test runner dependency at all. The scripts block has `test:e2e`, `test:stress`, `test:load`, `test:release` and nine `check:*` gates.
- `scripts/test/release-derive.test.mjs` is the only non-browser test in the repo, run under `node --test` via `npm run test:release`.
- Eight pure-logic suites are smuggled through Playwright as `e2e/*.unit.spec.ts`: `a11y-ci-gate`, `availability-slots`, `duplicate-detection`, `email-groups-footer`, `meeting-link-hybrid`, `notification-link`, `notification-text`, `unsubscribe-token`. The header of `e2e/unsubscribe-token.unit.spec.ts:1-8` states the reason outright: *"Playwright resolves the tsconfig `@/` paths, which `node --test` cannot."*
- `playwright.config.ts:35-59` runs `workers: 1` with a 60s timeout, so these eight suites are serialised behind a browser launch on every PR.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:19-111` has lint, `tsc --noEmit`, nine `check:*` scripts and `npm run build`; there is no unit test step to add coverage to.

## 🛠 What to build
1. Add **Vitest** (`vitest` + `@vitejs/plugin-react` if component tests are wanted later) with a `vitest.config.ts` that resolves the `@/` alias from `tsconfig.json`, uses the `node` environment by default, and includes `src/**/*.test.ts` + `src/**/__tests__/**`.
2. Add `npm run test:unit` (and `test:unit:watch`, `test:unit:coverage`).
3. Move the eight `e2e/*.unit.spec.ts` files next to the code they test, rewriting `import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test'` to the Vitest equivalents. Delete the originals so the Playwright suite stops paying for them.
4. Add coverage (`@vitest/coverage-v8`) with **per-module thresholds** on the modules Waves 0–1 rewrite, rather than one meaningless global number.
5. Wire `npm run test:unit` into `.github/workflows/ci.yml` as a required step before `npm run build`.
6. Document the runner in `docs/testing.md` — what belongs in a unit test vs. an e2e spec, and the rule that a new pure module ships with unit tests.

## ✅ Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `npm run test:unit` runs green locally and in CI in under 30 seconds
- [ ] No `e2e/*.unit.spec.ts` file remains; `npx playwright test --list` shows the suite shorter by those eight files
- [ ] Coverage thresholds fail the build when a listed module drops below its floor
- [ ] `docs/testing.md` documents the runner and the unit-vs-e2e rule
- [ ] `npm run build` passes
- [ ] a release fragment `releases/unreleased/<kebab-slug>.json` is added

## 🇹🇷 Türkçe özet
Bugün saf bir fonksiyonu test etmek için tarayıcı açmak gerekiyor; sekiz saf mantık testi sırf `@/` yollarını çözebildiği için Playwright'ın içine saklanmış durumda. Vitest kuruyoruz, o sekiz dosyayı `src/` altına taşıyoruz ve Dalga 0-1'in yeniden yazacağı modüllere (orgContext, entitlements, planGate, pipeline, dormantFirstContact) modül bazlı kapsam eşiği koyuyoruz. Bu olmadan migration, tenant anahtarı ve yetki modeli refaktörlerinin doğru olduğunu kanıtlamanın tek yolu tarayıcıda tıklamak.

## 🤖 Agent prompt
```
Objective: give this repo a unit test runner for src/ and coverage on the modules the
foundational refactors touch. Two child tasks; ship them in order.

Open first: package.json, tsconfig.json, playwright.config.ts, .github/workflows/ci.yml,
e2e/unsubscribe-token.unit.spec.ts (read its header — it explains why these live under e2e/),
docs/testing.md.

Constraints:
  - The `@/` path alias comes from tsconfig.json; vitest needs it wired explicitly or every
    moved test fails on import.
  - Do NOT import src/lib/prisma.ts or anything that pulls @prisma/client into a unit test —
    keep unit tests pure. Anything needing a DB stays in e2e/.
  - k6/*.js is deliberately outside tsconfig include; do not pull it into vitest either.
  - CI budget matters: the PR gate is ~2 min today. Keep test:unit under 30s.

Done when: npm run test:unit is a required CI step, the eight e2e/*.unit.spec.ts files are gone,
coverage thresholds exist per module, docs/testing.md explains the split, PR merged green.
```

**Zorluk** · M · **Tahmini** · 2-3 days · **Bağımlılık** · yok

records.title: feat(health): propagate required dependency state
records.body:
## Goal
Make final homelab health topology-aware so a service cannot appear fully healthy solely because its own App/container is `RUNNING` while a declared **required** dependency is unhealthy.

## Contract
Keep three distinct states in the API payload:
- `local_state`: direct service evidence (HTTP/application probe, TrueNAS runtime/container, internal probe, Cloudflare evidence)
- `dependency_state`: aggregation of outgoing `service-topology.json` relations with `strength=required`
- `effective_state`: final state consumed by FastAPI UI and downstream `nabla-site-alban`

Expose at least:
- `required_dependencies`
- `blocked_by`
- `dependency_evidence` with target ID, target state and relation type
- stale/observation-age evidence

## Semantics
- local/direct failure always remains fail
- locally healthy/running + failed required dependency becomes degraded/warn unless the service's own application-level probe also fails, then fail
- unknown/stale required dependency evidence must not yield green
- optional relations never downgrade effective state alone
- required-edge cycles/SCCs must be detected and surfaced, never recursively loop
- preserve raw/local evidence alongside propagated state so UI can explain the color

## Required regression cases
- Langfuse -> PostgreSQL + ClickHouse + Redis + MinIO
- n8n -> PostgreSQL
- LiteLLM -> Ollama
- Open WebUI -> LiteLLM
- STOPPED TrueNAS App with empty `active_workloads` must still reconcile to its declared service rather than split into `declared_only` + `observed_only`

## UI follow-up
FastAPI health board should show `RUNNING but degraded`, `blocked by …`, evidence source, age/stale state, and the distinction between runtime/local state and propagated effective state. Keep FastAPI lightweight; richer React Flow rendering belongs in `nabla-site-alban`.

records.title: Epic — production GraphRAG: truthful retrieval, grounded synthesis, and standing proof
records.body:
## Purpose

Finish GraphRAG as a production framework capability without creating a second owner for work already filed. This epic tracks the existing partition, readiness, retrieval-shape, summary-grounding, response-truth, payload-bound, and executable-proof issues. Each child retains its own design and acceptance authority.

This epic is unmilestoned. It is explicitly outside the capped `v1.0.0-beta.164` milestone and does not admit any child to a tag merely by listing it here.

## Existing owners

### Deterministic partition and availability

- [ ] #606 — replace LPA/fake hierarchy with the ruled prefix-derived partition and reconcile ADR-054 indexing eligibility before implementation
- [ ] #609 — retain only a currently reproduced cold-start/first-partition lifecycle gap after re-auditing the generation-safe query view

### Useful retrieval and grounded synthesis

- [ ] #823 — make sub-threshold global results useful to agent-facing consumers instead of dropping full-entity hits when digests are absent
- [ ] #829 — ground community summaries in entity content through the existing fetcher seam
- [ ] #701 — remeasure thematic recall after #606; implement bounded multi-community expansion only if the residual still exists

### Truthful and bounded contracts

- [ ] #1136 — distinguish result attribution from audited evidence and make GraphRAG documentation match admitted runtime behavior
- [ ] #839 — after #606 removes inline membership, retain only the independent bounded entity-batch request/response work used by GraphRAG hydration

### Standing executable proof

- [ ] #1117 — run the existing small-model semantic variant in the per-PR ladder as a path gate, not an unruled answer-quality gate

## Boundaries

- This epic does not reopen child designs, duplicate their acceptance criteria, or create a new GraphRAG implementation owner.
- Prefix-derived organization is not semantic community discovery. Any topology or semantic overlay is a separate future decision, gated by ADR-054/IndexProfile and filed only after a real post-#606 corpus measurement proves a specific remaining gap.
- The thematic evaluator remains a recorder. A quality-gate child is filed only after repeated measurements establish a stable metric, threshold, determinism envelope, runtime cost, and model-variant boundary. #1117 proves the executable path; it does not silently become a quality SLA.
- ADR-059 consolidates #213 and owns future audited claim/evidence retrieval: evidence refs, provenance, status, and confidence. #1136 owns truthful result attribution now. This epic does not implement audited evidence retrieval or relabel relevance as evidence confidence.
- Explicit relationship traversal remains PathRAG/graph topology. GraphRAG does not gain hop traversal or relationship-fed synthesis through this tracker.
- Raw KV and copied NATS subjects are not application fallbacks. Any new internal access uses an admitted operation or operation-specific typed adapter.

## Sequencing

1. Land #606's ruled partition and its ADR-054 reconciliation, with #1117 supplying standing semantic-path proof.
2. Re-audit/narrow #609 and #839 against the landed partition shape.
3. Land the independent contract and grounding defects #823, #829, and #1136.
4. Rerun the real thematic corpus; then resolve #701 as still-required, re-scoped, or obsolete by owner ruling.
5. File no topology-overlay or quality-gate child unless the measurements required above justify one.

## Completion

This epic closes only when every checked child is closed with its own owner-visible `CONFIRM-CLOSE`, or an owner ruling records that the child became obsolete and closes it under the same protocol. ADR-059/#213 remains a boundary, not an implicit unchecked child. Epic completion does not itself select a release candidate or alter milestone membership.

records.title: --exclude-filter removes all components for any .sln/.slnx/.slnf input, and for single-project input without --recursive
records.body:
# Summary

Passing any value to `--exclude-filter` — including a package name that doesn't exist in the dependency graph — causes the entire component list to be wiped out ("`Found 0 packages`") in two situations:
1. Any solution input (`.sln`, `.slnx`, `.slnf`), with or without `--recursive` (the flag has no effect here — see root cause).
2. A single project file (`.csproj` etc.) without `--recursive`.

It works correctly only for: a single project file with `--recursive`

Reproduced on `v6.2.0` (`latest`); traced back to the commit that introduced `--exclude-filter` (#939, 1615122, 2025-04-27) — present in every release since.

## Repro

### (1) Broken: solution filter, `--recursive` has no effect either way
  `dotnet-CycloneDX MySolution.slnf --disable-package-restore --exclude-filter "PackageThatDoesNotExist" --filename bom.json`
  `dotnet-CycloneDX MySolution.slnf --recursive --disable-package-restore --exclude-filter "PackageThatDoesNotExist" --filename bom.json`

### (2) Broken: single project, no `--recursive`
  `dotnet-CycloneDX MyProject.csproj --disable-package-restore --exclude-filter "PackageThatDoesNotExist" --filename bom.json`

### (3) Works: single project, with `--recursive`
  `dotnet-CycloneDX MyProject.csproj --recursive --disable-package-restore --exclude-filter "PackageThatDoesNotExist" --filename bom.json`

Cases (1) and (2) print, for every restored package:

The following orphaned packages have been removed:
    - <every single package>
  Found 0 packages

  Case (3) correctly prints `No orphaned packages were found.` and produces a full component list.

## Root cause

ExcludeFilterHelper.RemoveOrphanedPackages (ExcludeFilterHelper.cs) does a BFS starting only from packages with IsDirectReference == true, then intersects the package set with whatever's reachable:

  var queue = new Queue<DotnetDependency>(packages.Where(p => p.IsDirectReference));
  ...
  packages.IntersectWith(reachablePackages);

  This runs in Runner.cs right after packages are loaded:

  if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(options.DependencyExcludeFilter))
  {
      ExcludeFilterHelper.ExcludePackages(packages, options.DependencyExcludeFilter);
      ExcludeFilterHelper.RemoveOrphanedPackages(packages);   // ~line 251
  }

  But at this point in the flow, IsDirectReference has not been populated for most input types:

  - ProjectFileService.GetProjectDotnetDependencysAsync (the method used for a plain single project without --recursive, and also used internally, per-project, by the solution path below) never sets IsDirectReference on anything.
  - ProjectFileService.RecursivelyGetProjectDotnetDependencysAsync (used only for a single project with --recursive) does set it immediately on load — this is the one path that works.
  - For .sln/.slnx/.slnf input, Runner.cs branches to SolutionFileService.GetSolutionDotnetDependencys before ever checking --recursive (Runner.cs:171-182), so the flag has no effect for solutions at all. That method does contain logic that looks like it should propagate direct-reference
  status per project:

  // SolutionFileService.cs:185-199
  var projectPackages = await _projectFileService.GetProjectDotnetDependencysAsync(...);
  directReferencePackages.UnionWith(projectPackages.Where(p => p.IsDirectReference));
  ...
  foreach (var directPackage in directReferencePackages)
  {
      packages.TryGetValue(directPackage, out var package);
      package.IsDirectReference = true;
  }

  - but since GetProjectDotnetDependencysAsync never sets IsDirectReference in the first place, directReferencePackages is always empty and this block is effectively dead code.
  - The only place that actually populates IsDirectReference for these paths is Runner.cs's RemoveProjectReferencesAndMakeTheirDependenciesDirect(packages) call — but that runs after the exclude-filter block (~line 344 vs ~line 251).

  So for every input type except "single project + --recursive", the BFS starts from an empty set, and the filter step deletes everything.

  Suggested fix

  Ensure IsDirectReference is populated before the exclude-filter block runs, for all input types — e.g. by moving/duplicating the RemoveProjectReferencesAndMakeTheirDependenciesDirect call (or equivalent) earlier in Runner.cs, and/or fixing GetProjectDotnetDependencysAsync to set the flag
  on load so SolutionFileService's existing propagation logic actually does something.

  Environment

  - cyclonedx-dotnet (CycloneDX global tool) 6.2.0+55877e2ae058ae9686783ac084d2257d3fcedab1
  - .NET SDK 10.0.301
  - Reproduced against a single leaf .csproj, a single .csproj with --recursive, and a multi-project .slnf

  Related

  - #445 (a related but distinct issue: --exclude-dev correctly drops top-level PrivateAssets="All" packages but leaves their transitive-only children behind as orphans)

records.title: fix(core): search_files in tools.rs follows symlinks without cycle detection
records.body:
## Problem

The `search_files` function in `crates/cadis-core/src/tools.rs` (lines 1036-1074) recursively traverses directories using `fs::metadata`, which follows symlinks. While it checks `resolved.starts_with(workspace)` to prevent escaping the workspace, a symlink loop *within* the workspace (e.g., `dir/loop -> dir/`) causes infinite recursion and eventual stack overflow.

This is distinct from issue #743, which covers the `SearchIndex::build` function in `search_index.rs`. The `search_files` function in `tools.rs` is a separate code path used by the `file.search` tool handler.

## Actual Output

```rust
// crates/cadis-core/src/tools.rs:1059-1069
let Ok(resolved) = path.canonicalize() else { continue };
if !resolved.starts_with(workspace) { continue; }
let Ok(metadata) = fs::metadata(&resolved) else { continue };  // follows symlinks
if metadata.is_dir() {
    search_files(workspace, &resolved, query, max_results, matches);  // recurses into symlink target
}
```

If a workspace contains `ln -s . loopdir`, the function recurses into `loopdir` which resolves back to the same directory, causing infinite recursion.

## How to Fix

Use `symlink_metadata` instead of `metadata` to detect symlinks, and either skip symlinks entirely or track visited canonical paths to detect cycles:

```rust
let Ok(metadata) = fs::symlink_metadata(&resolved) else { continue };
if metadata.is_symlink() { continue; } // skip symlinks
```

Or use a `HashSet<PathBuf>` of visited canonical paths passed through the recursion.

## Expected Output

Symlink loops within the workspace do not cause infinite recursion or stack overflow. The search terminates normally.

## Critical Level

Medium

## My Confidence

High

## Why Matters?

The `file.search` tool is invoked by agent sessions, which are reachable from user and model input. A malicious or accidentally-created symlink loop in a project workspace would hang the daemon or crash it with a stack overflow, causing denial of service. The fix is straightforward and aligns with the existing symlink rejection in the SearchIndex module (#743).

records.title: Editing upstream Helix can retarget cylinder input to downstream pattern
records.body:
## Describe the bug

Codex-fuzzer-derived finding from authorized first-party browser/UI QA and follow-up codemod isolation on Zoo's owned modeling-app codebase. Browser/UI and AST rewrite behavior only; no credential inspection, vulnerability exploitation, network scanning, or third-party targeting.

Editing an upstream `helix(...)` operation that was built from a `cylinder = ...` input can recompute that cylinder input from the current artifact graph. If the original cylinder has a later downstream pattern child, the edit path can pick the downstream pattern instead of preserving the operation's original cylinder.

This is the same active codemod bug family as the upstream `translate(...)` and `patternLinear3d(...)`/`patternCircular3d(...)` edit findings: an edit should preserve hidden/implicit operation inputs unless the user explicitly retargets them.

## Steps to Reproduce

Minimal source-level reproduction:

1. Build an AST with this dependency shape:

   ```kcl
   extrude001 = extrude(profile001, length = 6)
   helix001 = helix(
     revolutions = 3,
     angleStart = 0,
     cylinder = extrude001,
   )
   pattern001 = patternLinear3d(extrude001, instances = 3, distance = 10, axis = X)
   ```

2. Build an artifact graph where the selected `extrude001` sweep has a downstream pattern child.
3. Call `addHelix(...)` with:
   - `nodeToEdit` pointing at `helix001`;
   - `cylinder` selection pointing at `extrude001`;
   - only visible/labeled Helix arguments changed, such as `revolutions` or `angleStart`.
4. Inspect the edited Helix call.

The current bug boundary is in `addHelix`: it uses `getVariableExprsFromSelection(..., nodeToEdit, { lastChildLookup: true })` for the cylinder argument even during an edit. That is unsafe for the same reason it was unsafe in Translate and Pattern 3D edits: the artifact graph can resolve the selected original input to a later descendant.

## Expected Behavior

Editing `helix001` should preserve the original cylinder input unless the user explicitly changes the cylinder selection:

```kcl
helix001 = helix(
  revolutions = 4,
  angleStart = 15,
  cylinder = extrude001,
)
pattern001 = patternLinear3d(extrude001, instances = 3, distance = 10, axis = X)
```

## Actual Behavior

The edit path is eligible to rewrite the cylinder reference to the later downstream pattern child:

```kcl
helix001 = helix(
  revolutions = 4,
  angleStart = 15,
  cylinder = pattern001,
)
pattern001 = patternLinear3d(extrude001, instances = 3, distance = 10, axis = X)
```

That changes the operation's dependency graph even though the user only edited Helix parameters. Depending on declaration order and operation semantics, this can create forward dependencies, cycles, or invalid downstream geometry.

## Source Evidence

Affected source on the PR investigation branch:

- `src/lang/modifyAst/geometry.ts`: `addHelix(...)` reconstructs the `cylinder` argument through `getVariableExprsFromSelection(...)`.
- The unsafe pre-fix behavior is the same `lastChildLookup` edit-time pattern previously isolated for `Translate` and Pattern 3D.

Local regression added during the Codex fuzzer follow-up:

```text
npm run test:unit -- src/lang/modifyAst.test.ts
```

The regression constructs `extrude001 -> helix001` plus a later `pattern001` child and asserts the edited Helix call keeps `cylinder = extrude001`, not `pattern001`.

## Expected Fix

When `nodeToEdit` is present, `addHelix` should not use last-child lookup to rebuild the existing cylinder input. Preserve the existing cylinder reference unless the command flow explicitly exposes and changes that input.

## Version

Observed against `origin/main` behavior during the 2026-08-28 Codex GUI-fuzz/codemod campaign.

## Duplicate Search

No open or closed issue matching `helix`, `lastChildLookup`, `nodeToEdit`, or the exact upstream Helix edit/descendant-retarget failure was found on 2026-08-28.

Related but distinct:

- #13391 covers `translate(...)`.
- #13394 covers Pattern 3D.
- #13248 covered the same edit-retarget class for upstream `hole::hole`.

records.title: Wire the existing `mix deps` result into dependency resolution
records.body:
Dependency resolution is done entirely by walking `mix.exs` files with the PSI parser
(`TransitiveResolution.transitiveResolution` → `Resolution` → `DepGatherer`). That walk cannot see
a dependency that no `mix.exs` declares, so **`rebar3` dependencies and everything beneath them are
never wired**.

Meanwhile the plugin already runs `mix deps` and already parses it, and that output lists every
dependency, flat, with its build tool.

## Observed

In a Phoenix project with 97 dependencies on disk, seven had no library order entry on the module:
`certifi`, `metrics`, `mimerl`, `nimble_ownership`, `parse_trans`, `ssl_verify_fun`,
`unicode_util_compat`. Confirmed with a debugger at `SyncPlanBuilder.buildModuleDepsPlan`: the
module's `deps` set held 138 entries and all seven were absent, so nothing downstream dropped
them — they were never resolved.

Six are `rebar3` dependencies of `hackney`, declared only in its `rebar.config`. `deps/hackney`
has no `mix.exs`, so `Resolution.rootVirtualFileToDepSet` finds no manifest, returns `emptySet()`,
and the walk stops there. `hackney` and `idna` are themselves found only because Elixir
dependencies name them in *their* `mix.exs`.

The consequence is not abstract: a path that needs `FilenameIndex` only resolves for a dependency
whose library is attached, so a stack-trace frame or a Go to File into an unattached dependency
silently does nothing.

## Proposal

Use `mix deps` as a first tier, unioned with the existing walk.

`PackageManager.depsStatus` already builds the command line, resolves the SDK, runs
`ExecUtil.execAndGetOutput` with timeout and cancellation handling, and parses the output with
`MixDepsStatusParser`. `DepsCheckerService` calls it from `DepsCheckerStartupActivity` and again on
every dependency change, caching per root. **No new subprocess, no new startup cost, and no new
trust exposure** — the data is already fetched and already parsed.

What is missing:

- **`MixDepsStatusParser.parseDepName` truncates at the first space**, discarding
  `(Hex package) (rebar3)`. The build tool is exactly the rebar signal, and the source distinguishes
  Hex from git and path dependencies. Both are on the line already.
- **`CachedRootStatus` discards the list.** It is `Ok | NonOk | Error | Unsupported`;
  `checkDepsStatus` receives the full `DepsStatus`, collapses it to `hasNonOk`, and drops every
  name. Retaining the list on the cache entry is the substantive change.
- **Paths.** `Dep` wants `deps/<name>`; `mix deps` does not print one. Correct for Hex and git
  dependencies and verifiable against disk, but path dependencies and umbrella apps — the ones that
  become `Dep.Type.MODULE` rather than `LIBRARY` — need care and a fixture.

## Read the cache, do not await it

`DepsCheckerService` subscribes to `ModuleRootListener.TOPIC` and calls
`scheduleTopologyAwareCheck("module roots changed")`. The sync's job is to *write* the module model,
so adding library entries fires `rootsChanged`, which schedules another check. Today the two are
independent and that is harmless. If the sync starts waiting on the check it becomes a loop —
sync → roots changed → check → sync — and the debounce softens it without breaking it.

So: the sync reads the cached list if present and falls back to the walk if not, and the check
requests a sync on completion rather than the sync waiting on the check. The dependency stays
one-way.

## Union, not preference

`mix deps` lists what is **locked**, so a dependency declared in `mix.exs` but not yet fetched does
not appear. `SyncPlanBuilder` deliberately keeps declared-but-unfetched dependencies so
`missingLibraryDeps` can create a placeholder — that is the state a project is in immediately after
someone adds a dependency. Both tiers are load-bearing.

## Worth checking while building

- Whether a `rebar3` dependency whose children are absent from `mix.lock` still appears.
- How long the subprocess takes on a cold project, since that sets how long tier one is missing
  after opening.

records.title: [Canonical Spec/PRD] 任务四一致性审核工作台目标产品合同与验收规格
records.body:
# Canonical status

**Status:** `CANONICAL` target-product contract; ready for `/to-tickets` decomposition after this issue and its three normative acceptance annexes are read together. The tracker has no `canonical` label, so canonicality is expressed by the issue title and this authority declaration; `ready-for-agent` means ready to decompose, not that this issue is one implementation ticket.

**Authority:** [Wayfinder map #1](https://github.com/Lijika/xiaopeng_comp/issues/1) and its final [canonical resolution](https://github.com/Lijika/xiaopeng_comp/issues/15#issuecomment-5150722545). This issue integrates, but does not reopen or replace, the accepted decisions in #2-#14 and ADR-0001-ADR-0008.

**Normative acceptance annexes:**

1. [Core contract and 14-state lifecycle matrix](https://github.com/Lijika/xiaopeng_comp/issues/16#issuecomment-5150838279).
2. [S01-S17 delivery-slice matrix](https://github.com/Lijika/xiaopeng_comp/issues/16#issuecomment-5150838454).
3. [A01-A14 migration/retirement matrix](https://github.com/Lijika/xiaopeng_comp/issues/16#issuecomment-5150838611).

The body plus those three comments form one specification. A row is complete only when every named evidence field and its release gate pass; prose, unit tests, screenshots, historical regressions, or reused code alone cannot satisfy a row.

## Problem Statement

Automotive-finance reviewers need one accountable place to determine whether the documents and field evidence within an application are mutually consistent, resolve uncertainty without overwriting machine conclusions, and hand a verification route to the separate disbursement-approval process. The current MVP demonstrates selected normalization, matching, rules, reports, adapters, and synthetic regressions, but its flat `Application -> RuleEngine -> Report` path has no authoritative application lifecycle, immutable evidence history, governed release, role-separated human decisions, durable concurrency/recovery semantics, or formal evaluation plane. Treating it as the product would lose provenance and overstate security and performance.

Current evidence also cannot support a real cross-document performance claim. There are 21 real motor-vehicle registration certificates and 97 images; Step2 covers 10 samples/44 page records, and OCR-derived artifacts cover 10 samples/40 actually processed pages. There is no real same-application multi-document corpus or independent ground truth. The 159 synthetic applications and 1,920 visible label pairs are development regressions, not an acceptance holdout.

## Solution

Build a **Consistency Review Workbench** whose unit of work and audit is one application. A registered source submits a versioned canonical envelope; the workbench atomically admits valid facts into an immutable evidence graph, derives one lifecycle-owned current state, freezes evidence and one governed policy release into each check run, and routes mandatory findings to automatic completion or accountable human work. Reviewers work from a queue into a finding-first, dual-pane application workspace; they can verify uncertainty, append corrections, request supplements, or request a separately approved exception. The workbench emits a verification route and durable downstream-delivery obligation, never a loan approval or rejection.

The target is a modular-monolith control plane with independent workers and an isolated evaluation runner. PostgreSQL owns structured facts, institution-controlled object storage owns attachments and large immutable artifacts, and all external surfaces are adapters around typed commands, immutable references, and minimized query DTOs. Public competition demonstration and controlled deployment share a pure domain/checking core but have separate identities, data, storage, networks, credentials, audit, and deployment manifests.

## Authority and conflict resolution

Load-bearing sources are: [#2 permissions](https://github.com/Lijika/xiaopeng_comp/issues/2#issuecomment-5146380668), [#3 evidence graph](https://github.com/Lijika/xiaopeng_comp/issues/3#issuecomment-5146727824), [#4 MVP inventory](https://github.com/Lijika/xiaopeng_comp/issues/4#issuecomment-5146875025), [#5 security](https://github.com/Lijika/xiaopeng_comp/issues/5#issuecomment-5147114184), [#6 lifecycle](https://github.com/Lijika/xiaopeng_comp/issues/6#issuecomment-5147415041), [#7 canonical input](https://github.com/Lijika/xiaopeng_comp/issues/7#issuecomment-5147876035), [#8 policy governance](https://github.com/Lijika/xiaopeng_comp/issues/8#issuecomment-5148058110), [#9 workbench UX](https://github.com/Lijika/xiaopeng_comp/issues/9#issuecomment-5148217432), [#10 evaluation](https://github.com/Lijika/xiaopeng_comp/issues/10#issuecomment-5148381533), [#11 architecture](https://github.com/Lijika/xiaopeng_comp/issues/11#issuecomment-5148537401), [#12 MVP disposition](https://github.com/Lijika/xiaopeng_comp/issues/12#issuecomment-5150263892), [#13 claims](https://github.com/Lijika/xiaopeng_comp/issues/13#issuecomment-5150376656), and [#14 delivery route](https://github.com/Lijika/xiaopeng_comp/issues/14#issuecomment-5150559546).

Resolution precedence is the final canonical resolution, then a later/more-specific accepted decision, then its accepted ADR; current source/tests describe implementation evidence only. Three apparent conflicts are resolved explicitly:

1. #4 recorded a historical full pytest/Web-smoke pass; #12 later recorded that the current 174-test collection stalled at a Web/KB TestClient case and that an independent Web smoke did not complete. The later #12 evidence controls: evaluator/probes may be cited only as `C-DEV-REG`; full HTTP/browser verification is `UNVERIFIED`.
2. #2 did not require WORM as the first logical audit owner; #11 later chose an independent append-only security audit ledger with complete asynchronous replication to an institution WORM/SIEM for controlled deployment. The ledger remains authoritative; the external copy is an integ
